claims.text: OC 186A introduces UPI Tap & Pay on Point of Sale (PoS) terminals as an additional mode for initiating UPI transactions alongside QR.
The enhancement enables Users to make contactless NFC-based UPI payments by unlocking their mobile device and tapping it on the PoS terminal.
UPI Tap & Pay transactions on PoS terminals are accepted only for Person-to-Merchant (P2M) transactions.
Payee PSPs must enable UPI Tap & Pay only on NFC-enabled PoS terminals certified in accordance with PCI PTS / CPOC standards.
UPI Application Providers and PSP Banks must obtain explicit User consent after each device binding operation before allowing further transactions.
Members and UPI Application Providers must obtain explicit User consent for enabling the UPI Tap & Pay feature, with Users having the ability to opt out at any time.
Payee PSPs shall integrate the Point-of-Sale Common Library for UPI (PoS CL) at the PoS terminal and complete integration on all terminals under its acquiring network.
UPI Application Providers must ensure device lock is enabled as a prerequisite for activating UPI Tap & Pay, and the device shall be unlocked at the time of initiating a transaction.
The per transaction limit for UPI Tap & Pay is capped at INR 5000, up to which additional factor of authentication shall not be required.
UPI Application Providers must ensure UPI Tap & Pay is made available through a dedicated call-to-action and presented as a standalone feature not embedded within other services.
Remitter Banks shall validate the User's account for UPI Tap & Pay feature enablement status before processing each transaction.
Members and UPI Application Providers shall be consulted to provide an option to Users to set their own transaction limits within the INR 5000 ceiling.
Settlement, reconciliation, dispute management, and Online Dispute Resolution for UPI Tap & Pay transactions must be carried out in accordance with extant UPI guidelines.
Members shall be guided by RBI guidelines on Harmonization of Turn Around Time (TAT) and customer compensation for failed transactions using authorized Payment Systems.
Members and UPI Application Providers shall refer to the applicable UPI Tap & Pay Feature Document, Technical Specifications and other instructions issued by NPCI for detailed requirements.

claims.text: OC 186A introduces UPI Tap & Pay on Point of Sale (PoS) terminals as an additional mode for initiating UPI transactions alongside QR.
The enhancement enables Users to make contactless NFC-based UPI payments by unlocking their mobile device and tapping it on the PoS terminal.
UPI Tap & Pay transactions on PoS terminals are accepted only for Person-to-Merchant (P2M) transactions.
Payee PSPs must enable UPI Tap & Pay only on NFC-enabled PoS terminals certified in accordance with PCI PTS / CPOC standards.
UPI Application Providers and PSP Banks must obtain explicit User consent after each device binding operation before allowing further transactions.
Members and UPI Application Providers must obtain explicit User consent for enabling the UPI Tap & Pay feature, with Users having the ability to opt out at any time.
Payee PSPs shall integrate the Point-of-Sale Common Library for UPI (PoS CL) at the PoS terminal and complete integration on all terminals under its acquiring network.
UPI Application Providers must ensure device lock is enabled as a prerequisite for activating UPI Tap & Pay, and the device shall be unlocked at the time of initiating a transaction.
The per transaction limit for UPI Tap & Pay is capped at INR 5000, up to which additional factor of authentication shall not be required.
UPI Application Providers must ensure UPI Tap & Pay is made available through a dedicated call-to-action and presented as a standalone feature not embedded within other services.
Remitter Banks shall validate the User's account for UPI Tap & Pay feature enablement status before processing each transaction.
Members and UPI Application Providers shall be consulted to provide an option to Users to set their own transaction limits within the INR 5000 ceiling.
Settlement, reconciliation, dispute management, and Online Dispute Resolution for UPI Tap & Pay transactions must be carried out in accordance with extant UPI guidelines.
Members shall be guided by RBI guidelines on Harmonization of Turn Around Time (TAT) and customer compensation for failed transactions using authorized Payment Systems.
Members and UPI Application Providers shall refer to the applicable UPI Tap & Pay Feature Document, Technical Specifications and other instructions issued by NPCI for detailed requirements.

claims.text: OC 186 originally required UPI Tap & Pay to be provided only through mobile devices having NFC capability.
OC 186A extends UPI Tap & Pay to Point of Sale (PoS) terminals enabling contactless payments by unlocking the mobile device and tapping it on the terminal.
OC 186 required UPI Apps to take permission from the customer to enable NFC for Tap & Pay transactions.
OC 186A requires explicit User consent after each device binding operation before allowing further transactions using UPI Tap & Pay.
OC 186 recommended having the App passcode, biometrics or pattern based lock in case of UPI LITE for small transactions.
OC 186A requires device lock to be enabled as a prerequisite for activating UPI Tap & Pay and the device must be unlocked at the time of initiating a transaction.

To ensure the safety and security of the UPI systems, NPCI constantly reviews the security checks of all components in the UPI ecosystem and regularly upgrades them to address evolving threats in cyber landscape. It provides ease of use, convenience and superior user experience with security and interoperability. To ensure the safety and security of the UPI systems, NPCI constantly reviews the security checks of all components in the UPI ecosystem and regularly upgrades them to address evolving threats in cyber landscape. There are security checks implemented as part of the code embedded in the Common Library (CL) along with the feature release to enhance user experience on UPI platforms. Integration of latest versions of CL is important to ensure enhanced security and safety in UPI ecosystem.
